1. (Currently amended) A composition, comprising: cavity-generating particles __selected from the group comprising nickel, copper, aluminum, silver, iron, brass and alloys, the cavity-generating particles being 100-200 μm in size__; a thermally conductive binder __comprising premixed solder paste__; and a solvent.

2. (Currently amended) The composition of claim 1, wherein the composition is applied to an electronic component surface.

3. (Currently amended) The composition of claim 2, wherein the solvent is removed during application to the electronic component surface.

4. (Original) A method of coating a surface whereby enhancing the boiling properties of the surface comprising the steps: creating a mixture comprising cavity-generating particles, a thermally conductive binder, and a solvent; applying a layer of the mixture to a target surface; heating the target surface, whereby the solvent is vaporized; and further heating the target surface, whereby the thermally conductive binder is melted.

5. (Original) The method of claim 4, wherein the layer is applied to the target surface using a paintbrush.

6. (Original) The method of claim 4, wherein the mixture is mixed using an ultrasonic bath.

7. (Original) The method of claim 4, wherein the solvent comprises ethyl alcohol whereby the target surface is first heated to vaporize the solvent.

8. (Original) The method of claim 4, wherein the target surface comprises an electronic component.

9. (Previously presented) A composition comprising cavity generating particles, a binder, and a carrier wherein the particle to binder ratio being about 1 gram to 0.5-0.8 grams and the carrier being about 10 ml per gram of particles.

10. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 9, wherein the carrier is selected from the group comprising ethyl alcohol, isopropyl alcohol, acetone, methylethyl ketone, FC-72, or FC-87.

11. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 9, wherein the binder is premixed solder paste.

12. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 9, wherein the cavity generating particles are selected from the group comprising nickel, copper, aluminum, silver, iron, brass and alloys.

13. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 9, wherein the cavity generating particles are 8-12 μm in size.

14. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 9, wherein the cavity generating particles are 30-50 μm in size.

15. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 9, wherein the cavity generating particles are 100-200 μm in size.

16. (Previously presented) A composition of matter comprising carrier, binder, and cavity generating particles, wherein said composition of matter contains, in relative proportion: about 10 ml carrier; about 0.5 to 0.8 grams binder; and about 1 gram of cavity generating particles.

17. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 16, wherein the carrier is selected from the group comprising ethyl alcohol, isopropyl alcohol, acetone, methylethyl ketone, FC-72, or FC-87.

18. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 16, wherein the binder is premixed solder paste.

19. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 16, wherein the cavity generating particles are selected from the group comprising nickel, copper, aluminum, silver, iron, brass and alloys.

20. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 16, wherein the cavity generating particles are 8-12 μm in size.

21. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 16, wherein the cavity generating particles are 30-50 μm in size.

22. (Previously presented) The composition of claim 16, wherein the cavity generating particles are 100-200 μm in size.

23. (Original) A method for surface enhancement to increase heat transfer of a surface in contact with a liquid, the method comprising applying to a surface the composition of claim 1.

24. (Original) The method of claim 23, wherein the composition is applied to the surface of an electronic chip.

25. (Original) An object to be immersed in a liquid coolant having a surface comprising cavity generating particles affixed by a binder such that boiling nucleation sites are formed in a density increasing critical heat flux of the surface.

26. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the cavity generating particles are selected from the group comprising nickel, copper, aluminum, silver, iron, brass and alloys.

27. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the cavity generating particles are 8-12 μm in size.

28. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the cavity generating particles are 30-50 μm in size.

29. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the cavity generating particles are 100-200 μm in size.

30. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the object is a microelectronic component.

31. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the object is a silicon chip.

32. (Original) The object of claim 25, wherein the liquid coolant is selected from the group comprising methanol, ethanol, fluorocarbons, water or FC-72.
